w: Interleukin-2 is for metastatic disease and carries significant toxicity.
Radiation is not effective for renal cell carcinoma, which is radioresistant.
p: Localized RCC is cured by partial or radical nephrectomy; metastatic disease needs targeted agents or checkpoint inhibitors.

w: Dabigatran needs 5-10 days of parenteral anticoagulation first, so it cannot start alone.
Aspirin is not adequate treatment for acute DVT.
p: Direct factor Xa inhibitors (apixaban, rivaroxaban) can be started immediately for DVT; provoked DVT usually needs 3 months.

bw: Solitary 5 cm brain mass with edema
w: Chemotherapy penetrates the blood-brain barrier poorly and is not the first step.
Whole-brain irradiation is for multiple metastases or inoperable lesions.
p: A solitary resectable brain metastasis in a patient with controlled systemic disease is treated with surgery, often followed by radiation.

x: first step debatable (nocturnal tumescence vs trial of PDE5 inhibitor)

w: Downey cells are atypical reactive lymphocytes of infectious mononucleosis.
Basophil predominance is seen in chronic myeloid leukemia, not in this immunodeficiency.
p: Chediak-Higashi: LYST mutation impairs lysosomal trafficking, causing giant granules, partial albinism, neuropathy and recurrent pyogenic infections.

w: Fluids are for hypovolemia, not a vigorous well newborn.
Silver nitrate is no longer used; erythromycin ointment prevents gonococcal conjunctivitis.
p: All newborns receive IM vitamin K (prevents hemorrhagic disease) and erythromycin eye ointment, plus hepatitis B vaccine.

x: asthma step-up regimen differs across guideline versions

w: Intracranial hemorrhage is not a typical ECT complication.
Acute coronary syndrome is a rare cardiac risk, not the usual side effect.
p: ECT commonly causes transient confusion and retrograde amnesia; it is the most effective treatment for severe or refractory depression.

bw: Mid-thoracic spine tenderness, high ESR and CRP
w: Herniated nucleus pulposus causes radicular pain without fever or raised inflammatory markers.
A muscle strain does not cause fever and leukocytosis.
p: Vertebral osteomyelitis (S. aureus in IV drug users) presents with focal back pain, fever and raised ESR; MRI is the best test.

w: Neurofibromatosis type 1 has smaller, smooth-bordered macules and neurofibromas but not precocious puberty with fractures.
Osteogenesis imperfecta causes fractures and blue sclerae without puberty or skin macules.
p: McCune-Albright: GNAS mosaic mutation causing polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots with irregular borders and endocrine overactivity.

bw: Burning leg pain with walking, relieved by rest
w: Arteriography is invasive and reserved for planning revascularization.
Venous duplex evaluates DVT or reflux, not arterial insufficiency.
p: Claudication from peripheral artery disease is screened with the ankle-brachial index (below 0.9 is abnormal).

w: Salicylates cause tinnitus, anion gap acidosis and hyperventilation, not marked transaminase elevation.
Tricyclics cause anticholinergic effects, QRS widening and seizures.
p: Acetaminophen overdose causes centrilobular hepatic necrosis with AST and ALT in the thousands by day 2-3; treat with N-acetylcysteine.

bw: Pregnant, flank pain radiating to groin
w: Noncontrast CT delivers fetal radiation and is second line in pregnancy.
A plain radiograph exposes the fetus and misses many stones.
p: Ultrasound is the first-line imaging for suspected nephrolithiasis in pregnancy; MRI or low-dose CT if inconclusive.

bw: Paraplegic, heel wound with pink base
w: Topical antibiotics treat infection but do not prevent pressure injury.
Heparin prevents DVT, not pressure ulcers.
p: Pressure ulcers result from sustained pressure over bony prominences; repositioning every 2 hours, pressure-relieving surfaces and skin care prevent them.

w: Temperature rises in serotonin syndrome, not the typical tyramine reaction.
Oxygen saturation is not the key danger in a tyramine reaction.
p: MAO inhibitors plus tyramine-rich foods cause hypertensive crisis with headache; treat with phentolamine or labetalol.

x: keyed 'preformed toxin' wrong for infant botulism (spores colonize gut)

w: Observation alone can miss serious esophageal injury, because symptoms do not predict damage.
Intubation is for airway compromise, which is absent.
p: Caustic ingestion needs early endoscopy (within 12-24 hours) even when asymptomatic; do not induce vomiting or neutralize.

bw: Mania after starting a new medication
w: Quetiapine treats mania and bipolar depression rather than provoking it.
Lithium is a mood stabilizer used to treat mania.
p: Antidepressants (SSRIs, TCAs) can precipitate mania or rapid cycling in undiagnosed bipolar disorder.

bw: Elderly, constipated, LLQ pain and fever
w: Lipase evaluates pancreatitis, not left lower quadrant pain.
Colonoscopy risks perforation in acute diverticulitis and is deferred for weeks.
p: Suspected acute diverticulitis is confirmed with CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast; colonoscopy follows after recovery.

bw: Diffuse calvarial uptake on bone scan
w: Paget disease usually has normal calcium unless the patient is immobilized.
PTH is normal; high PTH would suggest hyperparathyroidism.
p: Paget disease of bone: elevated alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium, phosphate and PTH; complications include deafness, fractures and osteosarcoma.
